decisions.reason: Encrypting and ownership-gating the PDF does not change its IPFS protocol, Pinata provider, hosting role, or client-removability semantics.

The source does not withdraw or revise the optional offline download; ownership verification can precede decryption or download without changing the existing availability and presentation requirement.
The source explicitly says the reader experience remains unchanged and does not alter the read-only default, PDF.js technology, or viewer entry points.
The metadata already points to an ownership-gated viewer rather than directly to the PDF; the Datil and encryption details do not change that metadata requirement.
The source configures ebook access gating and does not request any change to the About page's product, technology, process, feature, or vision copy.
The source establishes Lit Protocol implementation details but does not require corresponding FAQ copy changes.
Ebook ownership verification and Lit decryption do not change the referral commission amount, trigger, recipient, timing, limit, or payout mode.
Checking current Base ERC-721 ownership is compatible with book access transferring to a secondary buyer and does not alter any transferred NFT state.
The Lit Protocol access configuration does not affect no-referral commission allocation.
The source does not change ticket allocation when no referral code is used.
The source concerns ebook access infrastructure and does not revise landing-page hero wording or presentation.
Datil is the Lit Protocol production network, not a replacement for the Base blockchain; the source continues to require verification of Base ERC-721 ownership.
